science.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
science.summary: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.

science.summary: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage.

science.title: How one nuclear blast could cripple nearly every satellite in low Earth orbit
science.summary: We rely on satellites every day for communications, weather forecasts and security, and more than 13,000 are currently circling the planet in low Earth orbit. But they could be more vulnerable than previously thought. Researchers have found that a single nuclear explosion in space could disable almost all of them.

science.title: Quantum observers can 'agree to disagree,' but within limits, new theorem shows
science.summary: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments.

science.title: Meta-compass: An on-chip toolkit for visualizing optical spectrum and polarization
science.summary: A ruler turns length into a position on a scale. A thermometer converts temperature into the height of a liquid column. In each case, a physical quantity becomes easier to read because an instrument gives it a visible reference. We wanted to bring the same idea to light, whose properties are usually measured with separate optical components and then interpreted through additional data processing.

science.title: NASA, European sea level satellite prepped for new role
science.summary: As of Oct. 30, the Sentinel-6B satellite has been calibrated to serve as the world's go-to data source on sea level rise. The satellite has now passed all its initial system checks to ensure that its data meet the strictest quality and accuracy standards. In January, it will become the reference satellite that other sea-level missions use to calibrate their data.

science.title: Researchers count kinetochore proteins in living cells using an improved fluorescence-based method
science.summary: Accurate division of genetic material is critical for life and growth, and key to this is a protein structure called the kinetochore. science.title: Team extends a qubit's lifetime, correcting errors without measuring them
science.summary: Quantum technologies, devices that can process, store or collect information leveraging the laws of quantum mechanics, could potentially outperform their classical counterparts on some tasks. Yet these devices are highly sensitive to changes or disturbances in their surrounding environment, which can disrupt quantum effects and lead to errors.

science.title: New theoretical framework free of ghostlike instabilities expands the possibilities of symmetry in particle physics
science.summary: Elementary particles and the forces governing their interactions are described by relativistic quantum field theory, in which symmetry serves as a fundamental guiding principle. For more than half a century, the possible symmetries of such theories were believed to be restricted by the Coleman–Mandula theorem and its supersymmetric extension, the Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem.

science.summary: New research from the University of St Andrews, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, the North Coast Cetacean Society and Fisheries and Oceans Canada, has sequenced a whole whale genome using samples of "whale snot" collected by small drones off the coast of British Columbia—a world first.

science.summary: SpaceX brought back its Starship rocket's second stage today for a first-ever midair capture at its launch pad, capping a record-setting orbital flight test.
